title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (arranged for beginners)
subtitle: Traditional French melody, simple two-hand setting in 4/4
trains: A very well-known stepwise-and-small-leap melody in quarter and half notes, over a single sustained bass note per bar - an easy first tune for reading two staves together.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: The tune "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" is the French folk melody "Ah! vous dirai-je, Maman", first published c. 1761 from an earlier c. 1740 tune (public domain); the English nursery-rhyme text is Jane Taylor's 1806 poem, also public domain. The melody is the same one Mozart used, decades later, as the theme for his Twelve Variations K. 265 - the tune itself long predates and is independent of that set. Verified via the tune's Wikipedia history entry and the Wikipedia entry for Mozart's K. 265 variations.
provenance.note: A-B-A form in 12 bars of 4/4 (three 4-bar phrases; the last repeats the first), key of C major, quarter=92. The melody was checked against a 1918 printing of the song (see the audit record). The left-hand bass note per bar is our own simple setting.

departures: Key: C major (the 1918 printing it was checked against is in F).
The plain nursery-song form, not the ornaments of Mozart's K. 265 theme (bars 4, 6, 8 and 12).
Left hand: our own single bass note per bar; the printing has its own piano part.
